standout_why: Dashlore (cited) gives no power draw, cutoff voltage, battery-pack Wh or runtime. It only says to set a cutoff high enough to start the car. Dash Cam Empire (both parking pages) names a hardwire kit or battery pack with no numbers at all. RoadGearLab (uncited, rank 6) already does part of this: car-battery arithmetic (60 Ah battery with a 12.2 V cutoff gives about 18 Ah usable, about 32 h for an A229 Pro 3CH), the HK4 cutoff voltages and the B-130X recharge times (50 min hardwired, 90 min from the socket). But none of these pages turns recharge time into how long you have to drive per hour parked, and none says whether a daily commute keeps the pack topped up. Technobezz (cited) returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl, so I could not compare against it. The YouTube video (cited) was not checked. Hence 2, not 3.
kit_items: dash cam: VIOFO A229 Pro 2CH (4K front + 2K rear). rcg530 on DashCamTalk measured 4.98 W in low-bitrate parking, which is about 0.40 A at 12.6 V. A 12 h overnight park therefore uses 4.98 × 12 = 59.8 Wh, about 4.7 Ah from the car battery.

hardwire kit: VIOFO HK4 (Type-C, made for the A229 series). It has four selectable cutoffs: 11.8, 12.0, 12.2 and 12.4 V (RoadGearLab). Use 12.2 V or higher if the car sits for long periods. Amazon sells it bundled with the A229 Pro 2CH, so one ASIN covers both.

optional battery pack, for daily long parks or a weak or start-stop battery: VIOFO BP100. Vortex Radar measured 15 h 26 min of A229 Pro 3CH low-bitrate parking and a 63–70 min hardwired refill at about 113 W. Only buy it if daily driving is at least about 4.5 min per hour parked. Otherwise the pack never refills and you are back to relying on the car battery.
alternative camera for multi-day parking: Thinkware U3000. rcg530 measured 0.20 W in radar standby, against 4.98 W for the A229 Pro 2CH in low-bitrate mode. Over 48 h that is 9.6 Wh against 239 Wh.

findings.source_title: RoadGearLab: Best Dash Cam With Parking Mode 2026
findings.note: This is a rival page (rank 6), used because VIOFO's HK4 page returned HTTP 429. RoadGearLab's example: a 60 Ah flooded battery at about 80% charge with a 12.2 V cutoff leaves about 18 Ah usable. At 0.40 A (A229 Pro 2CH) that is 18 / 0.40 = 45 h before cutoff, a ceiling that cold weather and battery age shorten.
